## What's new

- **The interface does everything now.** Sign in, enter your R2 keys, add a
  folder, change what one includes, restore, rename, recover a deleted file,
  turn automatic backups on and off and change how often — all without
  leaving the window. Nothing tells you to go and run a command any more.

- **Four modes.** `1 Folders`, `2 Schedule`, `3 Trash`, `4 Account`, on
  number keys or <kbd>tab</kbd>. Scheduling in particular now has somewhere
  to live: what is registered, when it next runs, whether it runs while you
  are signed out.

- **Adding a folder means browsing to it.** No typing a path from memory —
  walk the disk, pick the folder, then untick what you do not want in the
  tree, then name it. It backs up straight away.

- **Every command still works exactly as it did.** The scheduler still runs
  `r2b backup`, your scripts are unaffected, and every flag means what it
  meant. The interface is a second front door, not a replacement.

## Fixed

- **The interface broke during its own backups.** Six seconds into any
  backup the progress screen was replaced by an error about a database file,
  and the app then believed nothing was running — so a second backup could be
  started on top of the first. The index was being opened twice in one
  process, and it locks against itself.

- **A restore ran with nothing on screen.** No bar, no phase, no title —
  just the folder list, until the result appeared minutes later.

- **The detail screen listed five keys that did nothing.** Back up, edit,
  restore, rename and "folder moved" are all live now.

- **A restore that matched nothing said it had worked.** A typo in "only
  paths matching" reported `0 restored` as an ordinary result. It is an
  error now, as it always was on the command line.

- **A bad folder name threw away the whole add flow** — browse, scan, pick,
  name, and only then rejected. Caught in the form now. This was the normal
  case on Windows when choosing a drive root.

- **You could not add a folder on another drive.** The browser could not go
  above `C:\`, and there was no way to type a path. Press `t`.

- **Hidden folders could not be reached** — `~/.config`, `~/.ssh` and the
  like. Press `.` to show them.

- **ctrl+c did not quit** from a form, a confirmation, or the folder browser.

- **A moved folder was not parked.** Backing one up from the interface left
  it looking healthy while the scheduled run failed every half hour.

- **Leaving mid-backup abandoned it.** Starting another job while a backup
  was running could wedge the upload partway with no sign anything was wrong.
  A second job is now refused while one is in flight, and the transfer can no
  longer be blocked by a screen that has gone away.

- **Layout on small terminals.** The frame could render a row taller than the
  window, which clipped the keyboard help off the bottom, and on an
  80-column terminal `q quit` scrolled off the end — a full-screen program
  with no visible way out.
